consensus_summary: The blind responses agree there is no settled biblical symbolism for 'west.' The most recognizable associations are (1) the setting sun, hence endings, decline, darkness, or death; (2) half of an east–west merism expressing totality or complete separation (Psalm 103:12); (3) the geographic/linguistic fact that Hebrew 'yam' (sea) means west, sometimes extended to Gentiles or the ends of the earth; and (4) a minority typological reading of westward movement as approach to God's presence in the tabernacle/temple.
book_summary: The book identifies west as 'where a course ends — behind, the destination.' Because Scripture's compass faces east, the western sea sits at one's back (the 'hinder sea'), and the Hebrew after/back/end word-family marks what is last, latter, or westernmost. East and west together span complete separation.
consensus_core_identification: No single settled meaning; the leading candidates are sunset-based ending/darkness/death, the east–west merism of totality/complete separation, and the geographic 'seaward' (yam) sense.
book_core_identification: West as the 'behind/end' direction — what is last, latter, hindermost, the terminus of a course — derived from the east-facing Hebrew orientation and the yam/'hinder sea' idiom, while retaining the east–west span as complete separation.
boundary_disagreement: The book grounds 'west = ending' not in the sunset (the consensus's dominant mechanism) but in bodily orientation: the east-facing observer has the west at his back, so west means 'behind, hinder, last.' It thereby drops the consensus's sunset-death-darkness-Satan strand and the minority 'westward toward God's presence' typology, while keeping the yam/sea identification and the Psalm 103:12 complete-separation merism. Cases like patristic baptismal renunciation facing west or west-as-darkness are excluded; cases like Joel 2:20's 'hinder part' and Jeremiah 50:12's 'hindermost' are newly foregrounded.
material_contradiction: None. 'Behind/end/destination' does not contradict any consensus identification; it reinterprets the ending theme through a different (linguistic-orientational) mechanism rather than replacing the referent.
rationale: The consensus admits no settled core, but its recognizable strands include ending/finality, the yam/sea linguistic sense, and complete separation via the east–west pair — all three of which the book retains. What the book changes is material: it unifies these strands under an orientation-based 'hinder/behind/last' logic, explicitly excluding the sunset-death-darkness reading that Responses A, C, and D treat as the best-known symbolic value, and ignoring the westward-approach-to-God typology. This is a real boundary and mechanism disagreement within the same general category (west as terminus/end), so REFINED with partial reclassification fits better than MATCH, DIVERGENT, or NOVEL.
strongest_objection: One could argue the book's identification is NOVEL: no blind response articulates the 'behind/hinder sea because the compass faces east' logic, and 'destination — where a course ends' is a distinct claim from sunset-based ending. However, Responses A and D both list 'completion, evening, or the end of a cycle' and 'finality, the close of an era' as recognized meanings, and B/C carry the yam/sea sense, so the book's category is covered even if its derivation is fresh.
